title: Thermal Design Engineer, Amazon Leo (Satellites)
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

We're looking for a Thermal Design Engineer who combines superb technical, research and analytical capabilities with a demonstrated ability to get the right work done quickly and effectively. This person must have experience working in spacecraft design, producing top notch thermal analysis and providing essential thermal related input and recommendations to vehicle architects and subsystem leads.

Key job responsibilities
- Support extensive architectural trades by performing preliminary thermal analysis of spacecraft and subsystems for orbital operational conditions and vehicle control options.
- Perform conceptual through detailed thermal analysis of Bus and Payload subsystems, components, and mechanisms.
- Support thermal design activities for additional future programs as the Amazon Leo constellation evolves.
- Develop automated scripts enabling rapid analysis updates to accommodate design trades (power states, duty cycles, structural mapping).
- Design, analyze, and select heat pipes for Bus and Payload components.
- Develop automated scripts enabling rapid analysis updates accommodating trades (power states, duty cycles, structural mapping).
- Define and execute thermal cycling and TVAC tests for development and qualification testing at the subsystem and vehicle level. Correlate test results with mission operations models.
- "Define and select test equipment as needed (e.g., sensors, data logging equipment).
- Perform thermal model correlation using test results.
- Conduct testing of prototypes and engineering models for fast design feedback loops.
- Plan and execute characterization, qualification, and acceptance tests.
- Document trades and design evolution, and prepare materials for design review gates.
- Support thermal design for terrestrial equipment and systems using CFD analysis.

About the team
Amazon Leo's Thermal Team is responsible for the thermal design solutions for all components in Amazon Leo's satellites and customer terminals. We work together with many engineering disciplines (e.g., mechanical, power, electrical, network, manufacturing) to find designs that maximize performance while minimizing mass, cost, and manufacturing complexity, and enabling all components to operate reliably over the satellite's target lifetime. The team follows all hardware components from conceptual design through detailed analysis, development testing, launch, and flight.

title: Senior TPM - Embedded Software, Amazon Leo
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. Export Control Requirement

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the embedded software for the Leo direct-to-device (DTD) payload system. This is a high-impact role where your work will directly influence how quickly and reliably we deploy the DTD constellation and enable service to our customers.

As a Senior Technical Program Manager, you will own the end-to-end technical program strategy for DTD payload embedded software, from architecture and design through verification and deployment.

Join us in shaping the future of satellite communications at Leo.



Key job responsibilities
As a Senior Technical Program Manager part of Amazon Leo DTD team, you'll lead technical program management of embedded software for the Leo DTD satellite payload, ensuring our Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) solutions perform flawlessly in real-world environments.

Drive programs from early architecture and design through integration and qualification testing, ensuring these critical systems meet performance, reliability, and schedule requirements. You'll develop mechanisms and processes connecting Leo engineering and business teams, software vendors and partners to build the Leo NTN solution.

Serve as the central program leader across a diverse set of cross-functional teams—from business development, communication systems, software engineering, to systems integration and test, manufacturing and production operations —to deliver payload software for Leo NTN solution.

Success requires deep technical judgment, strong program leadership, and the ability to drive alignment across complex engineering organizations. You will align teams across organizations, remove obstacles, and ensure complex technical programs move forward with speed, clarity, and accountability.

Develop and maintain program plans that track major milestones across feature development, design reviews, integration activities, qualification testing, and end-to-end network readiness. You will proactively identify technical and programmatic risks, build mitigation strategies, and communicate clear status updates to engineering leaders and stakeholders to ensure alignment across the organization.

Help transition from early development of DTD payload software to large-scale DTD solution supported by the Leo DTD constellation, device ecosystem and core networks. You will collaborate with engineering teams, manufacturing and production operations as well as software vendors, and test equipment vendors to scale the production of DTD satellites. This includes managing performance, reliability, and test automation of payload embedded software.

Assessment * Based on preliminary screening of patients, initiates assessment of patients chronic disease management needs and psychosocial risk factors and availability of resources to assist upon discharge. * Partners with the PAS, financial counselor and/or UM nurse to assess insurance and coverage requirements for all payers to ensure adherence to those requirements. * Collaborates with the patient and family, along with the physician(s) and other members of the care team to fully establish and support both the patients care progression and discharge plans.. * Meets with physicians and care team routinely to collaborate on timely and efficient patient management. title: Structural Engineer -Temporary Structures
description:
The Structural Engineer- Temporary Structures is a mid-level engineering role based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, supporting the design and delivery of temporary structural systems across construction and event-related projects. This position contributes to engineering design, analysis, and on-site verification of systems such as scaffolding, shoring, and formwork within a multidisciplinary project environment.

The role spans multiple project phases, including conceptual design, detailed engineering, construction support, and field inspection, ensuring compliance with applicable Canadian building codes and health and safety standards. Work includes coordination with construction teams, project managers, and design stakeholders to deliver safe and buildable temporary structure solutions.

The ideal candidate has approximately 5+ years of experience in structural engineering with direct exposure to temporary works design, strong analytical capability, and working knowledge of structural software and regulatory frameworks.

Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Design and analyze temporary works systems including scaffolding, shoring, and formwork using structural engineering principles
  • Perform structural calculations and modelling to validate stability, load capacity, and code compliance
  • Develop detailed engineering drawings and technical specifications for temporary structures
  • Conduct site inspections and construction monitoring to verify compliance with design drawings and safety standards
  • Provide technical support to construction teams during erection and dismantling phases of temporary works
  • Coordinate with project managers, architects, and engineers to integrate temporary structure solutions into project delivery
  • Prepare technical reports, engineering documentation, and design submissions for internal and external stakeholders
  • Review installation practices and identify risks related to structural integrity, constructability, and site safety
  • Ensure all engineering work aligns with applicable health and safety regulations and industry standards
  • Maintain awareness of advancements in temporary works design, materials, and construction methodologies

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related discipline
  • Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) designation or eligibility for registration in Ontario
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in structural engineering, including temporary works design
  • Proficiency with structural analysis software such as SAP2000, STAAD Pro, or RISA
  • Experience with CAD software including AutoCAD and/or Revit
  • Knowledge of Canadian building codes, engineering standards, and construction regulations
  • Experience performing structural calculations, design verification, and site inspections
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical reporting skills
  • Valid driver’s license with availability for site visits

Assets

  • Certification in scaffold design and safety
  • Experience supporting infrastructure or heavy construction projects
  • Familiarity with construction sequencing and temporary works planning
  • Exposure to multidisciplinary project coordination environments
  • Advanced degree in structural engineering or related field

title: Senior TPM - 3GPP NTN Verification and Validation, Amazon Leo
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access.

Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the Leo direct-to-device (DTD) system integration, verification, and validation. This is a high-impact role where your work will directly influence how quickly and reliably we deploy the DTD constellation and enable service to our customers.

As a Senior Technical Program Manager on the DTD TPM team, you will own the end-to-end technical program strategy for DTD systems integration, verification, and validation.

Join us in shaping the future of satellite communications at Leo.

Key job responsibilities
As a Senior Technical Program Manager part of Amazon Leo DTD team, you'll lead technical program management of DTD systems through integration, verification, and validation, ensuring our Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) solution performs flawlessly in real-world environments.

Drive programs from early architecture and design through integration and qualification testing, ensuring these critical systems meet performance, reliability, and schedule requirements. You will develop mechanisms and processes connecting Leo engineering, business, and production teams to ensure the Leo NTN solution meets the requirements for our customers.

Serve as the central program leader across a diverse set of cross-functional teams—from business development, communication systems, networking software, to systems integration and test – to ensure the DTD solution, including satellite payload and network connectivity, is delivered to meet performance requirements and quality standards

Success requires deep technical judgment, strong program leadership, and the ability to align complex engineering organizations.

Develop and maintain program plans that track major milestones across integration activities, qualification testing, system readiness and deployment. You will proactively identify technical and programmatic risks, build mitigation strategies, and communicate clear status updates to engineering leaders and stakeholders to ensure alignment across the organization.

Help transition DTD payload development from early integration into a large-scale solution supported by the Leo DTD constellation, device ecosystem, and core networks. You will take ownership of systems-level integration, verification, and validation.

title: Surgery Field Engineer Apprentice
description:
Job Description Summary

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to create a world where healthcare has no limits. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

In this role, the Field Engineer Apprentice will observe and perform various equipment service processes and procedures to drive customer satisfaction and ensure proper functionality of less complex customer diagnostic imaging equipment. This is an onsite customer‑facing service position focused on maintaining and repairing medical equipment in healthcare environments. Time is spent supporting customers in hospitals and clinical settings, serving as the face of GE HealthCare at customer sites in Austin, TX or San Antonio, TX.

This one-year apprenticeship is designed to prepare candidates for long‑term career in field service. The apprenticeship will be scheduled to align with the anticipated availability of an internal position to support continuity of employment following program completion.

Job Description

Responsibilities

  • Work within hospital radiology environment to evaluate and troubleshoot imaging equipment issues and implement appropriate repairs.

  • Complete Preventative Maintenance on designated equipment.

  • Perform safety and environmental inspections ensuring compliance to Health and Human Services and Environmental Health and Safety guidelines.

  • Complete necessary service and repair documentation following hospital protocol and GEHC policies & procedures.

  • Maintain daily communications with customers to ensure resolution and proper follow-up, leading to customer satisfaction.

  • Learn and ensure proper care of tools and test equipment and ensure calibration. Enhance and maintain technical knowledge of current standards, codes and procedures regarding safe and effective use of medical equipment.

  • Mentor with and assist more experienced technicians on progressive repairs and resolution, and will work as a member of the local team to provide efficient service delivery to all accounts within his/her assigned area

  • Complete all planned Quality and Compliance training within the defined deadlines. Identify and report all customer quality or compliance concerns immediately to the Quality Organization.

  • Aware of and comply with the GEHC Quality Manual, Quality Management System, Quality Management Policy, Quality Goals, and applicable laws and regulations as they apply to this job type/position.

Work Environment & Travel

  • Field roles are most effectively performed outside of GE HealthCare facilities and generally take place at customer locations, including hospitals and healthcare environments.

  • Healthcare operations run 24/7. Apprentices must be flexible to support customer needs, which may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, or adjusted hours based on service or customer requirements.

  • Travel to customer locations may be required, depending on market and business needs.

Required Qualifications

  • AS, BS degree, military education, certificate program, current student with less than 12 months from completion OR High School Diploma/GED with 6 months experience servicing electronic, IT or mechanical equipment.

  • Must have reliable transportation and a valid driver's license.

  • Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job.

Desired Qualifications

title: Wastewater Modeller

Join Egis and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of sustainable water infrastructure across the UK.We are committed to our planet

In each project we design, engineer and operate we care deeply about the legacy we’re leaving behind. As part of our team, you’ll have a unique opportunity to use your skills and expertise to shape a better future for our communities in the UK, and all around the globe.

About This Job

The Portfolio Associate supports Credit and Portfolio Management within the Fund Finance portfolio, managing a portfolio of subscription credit facilities and related lending products using a risk-based approach. This role is responsible for ongoing portfolio monitoring, transaction execution support, and financial analysis, while ensuring adherence to lending policies, documentation standards, and regulatory requirements.

Responsibilities:
  • Review and validate Post Funding Covenant (PFC) audits, borrowing base certificates and loan/line advances. Escalating any complex issues or exceptions to management
  • Conduct comprehensive loan reviews, collection of financial statements, financial statement spreading and the financial analysis of borrowers
  • Routine monitoring of commercial credits by way of covenant tracking, servicing borrower inquires, and facilitating the gathering of essential portfolio data is essential
  • Perform reporting and analysis on lending portfolio including monthly and quarterly data reports
  • Maintain electronic loan files and prepares reporting on trends, ratios, and cash flow analysis
  • Consult with customers to verify financial and credit transactions; respond to customer inquiries and resolves customer complaints
  • Lead, develop and train Portfolio Analysts and Associates

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field
  • 2+ years of experience in portfolio management, credit underwriting, or structuring within commercial lending, preferably with exposure to fund finance or specialty finance
  • Strong understanding of lending structures, financial analysis, and credit risk principles
  • Experience with borrowing bases, covenants, and loan documentation
  • Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills
  • Ability to operate independently and manage deadlines in a high-volume environment
